briefdescription.para: Print the current type.

detaileddescription.para: Omit the type details if NoDetails == true. E.g., let st = type { i32, i16 } When NoDetails is true, we only print st. Put differently, NoDetails prints the type as if inlined with the operands when printing an instruction.

briefdescription.para: Return true if this is 'void'.
Return true if this is 'half', a 16-bit IEEE fp type.
Return true if this is 'bfloat', a 16-bit bfloat type.
Return true if this is a 16-bit float type.
Return true if this is 'float', a 32-bit IEEE fp type.
Return true if this is 'double', a 64-bit IEEE fp type.
Return true if this is x86 long double.
Return true if this is 'fp128'.
Return true if this is powerpc long double.
Return true if this is a well-behaved IEEE-like type, which has a IEEE compatible layout as defined by APFloat::isIEEE(), and does not have non-IEEE values, such as x86_fp80's unnormal values.
Return true if this is one of the floating-point types.
Returns true if this is a floating-point type that is an unevaluated sum of multiple floating-point units.

detaileddescription.para: An example of such a type is ppc_fp128, also known as double-double, which consists of two IEEE 754 doubles.

briefdescription.para: Return true if this is X86 AMX.
Return true if this is a target extension type.

detaileddescription.para: For example, i8* to i32*. BitCasts are valid for types of the same size only where no re-interpretation of the bits is done. Determine if this type could be losslessly bitcast to Ty

briefdescription.para: Return true if this type is empty, that is, it has no elements or all of its elements are empty.
Return true if the type is "first class", meaning it is a valid type for a Value.
Return true if the type is a valid type for a register in codegen.

detaileddescription.para: This includes all first-class types except struct and array types.

briefdescription.para: Return true if the type is an aggregate type.

detaileddescription.para: This means it is valid as the first operand of an insertvalue or extractvalue instruction. This includes struct and array types, but does not include vector types.

briefdescription.para: Return true if it makes sense to take the size of this type.

detaileddescription.para: To get the actual size for a particular target, it is reasonable to use the DataLayout subsystem to do this.

briefdescription.para: Return the basic size of this type if it is a primitive type.

detaileddescription.para: These are fixed by LLVM and are not target-dependent. This will return zero if the type does not have a size or is not a primitive type.
If this is a scalable vector type, the scalable property will be set and the runtime size will be a positive integer multiple of the base size.

Note that this may not reflect the size of memory allocated for an instance of the type or the number of bytes that are written when an instance of the type is stored to memory. The DataLayout class provides additional query functions to provide this information.

briefdescription.para: If this is a vector type, return the getPrimitiveSizeInBits value for the element type.

detaileddescription.para: Otherwise return the getPrimitiveSizeInBits value for this type.

briefdescription.para: Return the width of the mantissa of this type.

detaileddescription.para: This is only valid on floating-point types. If the FP type does not have a stable mantissa (e.g. ppc long double), this method returns -1.

briefdescription.para: Return whether the type is IEEE compatible, as defined by the eponymous method in APFloat.
If this is a vector type, return the element type, otherwise return 'this'.
Get the address space of this pointer or pointer vector type.
Just like llvm::Type these are immutable, unique, never get freed and can only be created via static factory methods.
